ingredients.item: Shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Drain and rinse the beans, drain the olives, chop the bell pepper and green onions, chop the tomato and shred the lettuce.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook for about 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink is left. Spoon off any extra fat.
Add the beans, the salsa and the taco seasoning. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it's hot.
Break the tortilla chips into pieces. Spread 1 1/4 cups of them over the bottom of an 8x8 inch baking dish.
Spoon the beef mixture over the chips. Scatter the bell pepper, the green onions, the olives and the cheese on top.
Bake, uncovered, for 20 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Top with the tomato, the lettuce and the remaining 1/4 cup broken chips. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Keep the lettuce and tomato off until you serve.
method_notes: Amanda's Cookin' is the lead (5 from 44): taco-seasoned beef with black beans and salsa, spooned over broken tortilla chips, topped with vegetables and cheese, baked at 350°F for 20 minutes, then finished with fresh tomato, lettuce and a few more chips. The source makes 8 servings; this is cut in half. Other versions layer tortillas or refried beans instead of chips; this one keeps the chips because the lead does. The base is mild, and there is no chili in it.
